🗓 **TAWG Daily Catch-up**
_2026-11-05 23:00 → 2026-11-06 23:00 UTC_

## ⚡ **Highlights**

> **Two routes, one verifier home** — the on-chain verifier repository now carries a zero-knowledge path and a committee attestation path side by side. [commit a5d554f](https://github.com/trustless-ai/flashprove-onchain-verifier/commit/a5d554fcc3378702c25f63d25492381631b4b4fa)

> **Committee attestation took shape** — a k-of-n path grew from a starter frame into a working committee signature check. [PR #1](https://github.com/trustless-ai/flashprove-onchain-verifier/pull/1)

> **An independent check landed** — a separate ERC-8274 claim-boundary experiment shared a 54/54 result with the group. [tg:tawg:6203]

## 🤝 **What moved**

### on-chain verifier
_The verification effort gained one home with room for both proof routes._

- Jimmy Shi **Restructured** the repository around the on-chain verifier so the deployment is treated as the product, giving both proof routes a shared foundation. [commit 71a48e9](https://github.com/trustless-ai/flashprove-onchain-verifier/commit/71a48e9691d08fbd8f37bc3f1f483d3cd9c60375)
- Jimmy Shi (@jimmyshi) **Opened** the new flashprove-onchain-verifier repository to Fede with the zero-knowledge and multi-sig attestation routes together, which keeps the two approaches comparable in one codebase. [tg:tawg:6193]

### attestation
_The committee route advanced from an outline to reviewed code._

- Baby Blue Viper **Implemented** the k-of-n path with EIP-712 typed data binding signers to the input, output, and metadata hashes, turning the outline into something the group can test. [tg:tawg:6213]
- Pavlo **Reviewed** the change and confirmed that the EIP-712 binding, distinct-signer counting, and negative controls address the main attestation concerns, giving the group a clearer signal for the next step. [review comment](https://github.com/trustless-ai/flashprove-onchain-verifier/pull/1#issuecomment-6683995010)
- Jimmy Shi (@jimmyshi) **Sketched** the k-of-n frame for Fede, removing the blank-page cost and letting attestation work start right away. [tg:tawg:6198]

### zero-knowledge
_The zero-knowledge side is staged for a live run._

- Jimmy Shi (@jimmyshi) **Flagged** the zk verifier as ready for a real run and pointed Merlini to that exact contract for GPU time, setting up an end-to-end check of the other route. [tg:tawg:6201]
- Jimmy Shi **Opened** a no_std Rust port of FlashProve cp_verify as an ERC-8274 verifier draft, extending the proof logic toward on-chain environments. [FlashProve PR #1](https://github.com/trustless-ai/FlashProve/pull/1)

## 🚀 **Next up**

### 💡 **Ideas to follow**

- A Magicians thread follow-up pairs the ERC-8183 discussion with a reference described as MIT-licensed, pre-audit, and local-tests-only, worth reading with that caveat in view. [post #443](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/erc-8183-agentic-commerce/27902/443)
- Another note points to the eip.md in erc-8183/base-contracts at revision 142e669 as a cross-reference worth checking against the thread. [post #447](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/erc-8183-agentic-commerce/27902/447)

### ✅ **TODOs**

- Run the zero-knowledge verifier on GPU-backed hardware and capture its results against the attestation route.
- Fold the k-of-n review notes into the verifier interface documentation so both routes share one contract.
- Reconcile the independent claim-boundary findings with the repository's current test coverage.

## 🤖 **Trusty's take**

> **Today's spark:** A rough k-of-n frame became reviewed attestation code as the day unfolded, turning a sketch into a shared working loop.
>
> Keep the relay rolling — good handoffs make the next lap lighter. 🔄
